By code reading, a second trigger: a beta.12 protocol-1 encrypted payload (ciphertext inside data, re-encrypted with a fresh IV per upload) accepted by a server without required encryption or with allowPlaintextMigration is refused FORGED_DUPLICATE on every re-upload. Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-84.test.ts (memory store; same code path on every store). Required fix: compare a duplicate against what the client SENT, not what the server stored after rewriting it: persist the as-uploaded identity (or its content key) beside a transformed copy, or compare a transformed stored copy on (id, node, sequence, type, collection, recordId, timestamp) only; never treat a body the server itself rewrote (transform, restored legacy data, protocol-1 ciphertext) as evidence of forgery. FIXED (Phase 3 round 5, root cause, 2026-10-03, branch worktree-agent-a2ac5bc3753e8df53, commits 1a134ab, a012d57). Root cause: the server stored a schema-transformed REWRITE under the original id (an immutable, content-addressed operation mutated after creation). Transforms now run at fold time: the server stores every upload exactly as uploaded (all hashed fields, hashVersion, envelope; plus only the verified hash-version declaration and a beta.12 clear made explicit, both identical under the id) and delivers that original; core operationSchemaView is the one place transforms run (server authorization, validators, constraint checks, scope filters, every server store fold via ServerStore.setOperationTransforms / setSchema options, every device fold via StoreConfig.operationTransforms from createApp). FORGED_DUPLICATE now compares against the as-uploaded copy; copies earlier releases rewrote (no hashVersion and an id that does not verify against their own body, incl. protocol-1 ciphertext) compare on id, node, type, collection, record and timestamp (duplicate-identity.ts isSameOperationAsStored); a device echoing another node's operation that its earlier build stored rewritten is acknowledged as a duplicate (isRewrittenEcho). Transforms must be pure and deterministic (identity changes refused SCHEMA_TRANSFORM_INVALID) and are part of the fold plan fingerprint (server and client). Tests: repro RT-84 (memory and Postgres), core migration/operation-view.test.ts, server protocol-v2-ingest.test.ts (stored as uploaded, delivered as uploaded to v1 and v2 clients, legacy rewritten copies, store re-fold on transforms), packages/test schema-version-convergence (old-schema clients receive each other's ops as written), fold gate mixed-schema sweep (200 seeds).

problems.title: A server schema transform that drops a field from an update's data now clears that field on the server and on every peer: the transformed copy is stored without hashVersion, and mergeOp folds every undeclared update with canonicalizeLegacyOperation (a previousData key absent from data is a clear)
problems.notes: Phase 3 red team round 4, 2026-10-03 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md, Round 4). Regression of the round-4 canonical body (commit 44f11ed: canonicalizeLegacyOperation applied in mergeOp) combined with transformForServerSchema stripping hashVersion. Locations: core/src/fold/fold.ts:398, core/src/operations/canonical-body.ts:260-270 (any op without hashVersion 2 and no envelope is 'legacy'), server/src/session/client-session.ts:2844-2861. The OperationTransform contract (core/src/migration/operation-transform.ts) and docs speak of rewriting data only; a transform that stops older clients from writing a field (delete data.score) leaves score in previousData, and every replica folds the stored copy as score: null. Before round 4 the copy did not touch score. Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-85.test.ts. Required fix: apply the legacy clear rule only to genuine beta.12 bodies (mark them at ingest, e.g. a 'legacy' body flag or hashVersion 1 declared by the server only when the id verified WITH the restore), never to server-transformed copies; or have transformForServerSchema drop from previousData every key the transform removed from data. FIXED (Phase 3 round 5, root cause, 2026-10-03, branch worktree-agent-a2ac5bc3753e8df53, commit 1a134ab). Root cause: the fold applied the beta.12 clear rule to every op without hashVersion 2, a property transformed copies share. The rule left mergeOp: a genuine beta.12 body is made canonical ONCE where its provenance is known, and stored canonical (null and undefined hash alike under v1, so the id is unchanged): server ingest of protocol-1 uploads (as before), a device's own undeclared updates at its one-time upgrade pass (store fold/legacy-bodies.ts), and any body whose id PROVES the clear (core canonicalizeProvenLegacyClear) on inbound delivery and in one-time passes over the client log and the SQLite/Postgres server logs (server store/legacy-bodies.ts, marker legacy_bodies_canonical). A transform runs on the as-uploaded body at fold time, after nothing, so a dropped field stays in previousData without ever being read as a clear. Tests: repro RT-85 (memory and Postgres), core operation-view.test.ts (fold applies no legacy rule; proven vs rewritten bodies), store legacy-bodies.test.ts, server legacy-bodies.test.ts (SQLite, Postgres), repro RT-83 still green, rt3-upgrade-clear-probe 3/3 + 6/6.

problems.title: A local write larger than the server's maxOperationBytes (default 256 KiB) is accepted by the API and then wedges the device's upload stream for good: the server answers with a session-level OPERATION_TOO_LARGE error and stops acknowledging the batch, the device re-sends it every session, and no later write of that device reaches the server or a peer
problems.notes: Phase 3 red team round 4, 2026-10-03 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md, Round 4). Not a round-4 regression (no client-side size check exists; the server path is older). Locations: server/src/session/client-session.ts:2560-2569 (validateOperationSize -> sendError('OPERATION_TOO_LARGE', ..., false) and canAdvanceAck = false, not a per-op operation-rejected), server/src/session/session-operation-limits.ts:4 (DEFAULT_MAX_OPERATION_BYTES 256 KiB); store/sync: no size check before the write is accepted. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-86.test.ts: a 300 KiB string field, then a small insert; after three reconnects the peer has neither, and A has no rejection recorded (the app is told nothing about which write is at fault). Required fix: refuse the oversized operation terminally and per operation (operation-rejected OPERATION_TOO_LARGE, retriable false, ack advances past it), and/or refuse it in the local API before it is written (the limit advertised in the handshake), so one write can never block every later one. FIXED (Phase 3 round 5, root cause, 2026-10-03, branch worktree-agent-a2ac5bc3753e8df53, commit 1a134ab). One value domain (core schema/value-domain.ts). maxOperationBytes is checked in the local write path (write-ops buildLocalOperation, same measure as the server: UTF-8 of the op JSON; OperationTooLargeError, nothing written; StoreConfig.maxOperationBytes / createApp store.maxOperationBytes, default 256 KiB = server default). The server refuses an oversized op per operation and terminally (operation-rejected OPERATION_TOO_LARGE, retriable false, ack past it): never a session error. Tests: repro RT-86, store mutations/value-domain.test.ts, server value-domain-ingest.test.ts and kora-sync-server.test.ts (inverted: per-op rejection, no session error), packages/test value-domain-roundtrip.test.ts (device limit above the server's: refused per op, reported, later writes sync, writer excludes the refused write).

problems.title: A t.timestamp() value the API accepts does not fit the Postgres server store's BIGINT column: a fractional timestamp is refused UNSTORABLE_VALUE and the record vanishes from the writing device; one beyond the BIGINT range (1e20) fails the batch unmapped and wedges the device's upload stream
problems.notes: Phase 3 red team round 4, 2026-10-03 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md, Round 4). Not a round-4 regression. Locations: core/src/schema/validation.ts (timestamp: any finite number), server/src/store/materialization.ts fieldTypeToSql ('timestamp' -> BIGINT on Postgres), server/src/store/postgres-server-store.ts:160-187 (PG_UNSTORABLE_VALUE_CODES = 22021, 22P05, 22P02: a fractional value fails 22P02 and is refused terminally; 1e20 fails 22003 numeric_value_out_of_range, not mapped, so the batch fails and is re-sent every session). Memory and SQLite server stores and every client store hold both values. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-87.test.ts (KORA_PG_TEST_URL): fractional -> A shows only the next write, rejection UNSTORABLE_VALUE; 1e20 -> B receives nothing, A has no rejection. Required fix: define the timestamp domain once and enforce it where the value is written (validateFieldValue: a safe integer, or round in the canonical body), so every store holds every accepted value; map every Postgres value refusal (SQLSTATE class 22) to a per-operation terminal refusal, never a failed batch. FIXED (Phase 3 round 5, root cause, 2026-10-03, branch worktree-agent-a2ac5bc3753e8df53, commit 1a134ab). One value domain (core schema/value-domain.ts, table in docs/guide/schema-design.md#value-domain): t.timestamp() = integer ms in [-8.64e15, 8.64e15] (fractions refused with a clear error, not rounded), t.number() finite, structured values depth <= 64, no __proto__ key, not exactly the wire's { __kora_bytes__ } form; enforced in validateRecord, after atomic ops resolve (assertResolvedFieldValue), and on server ingest of uploads and route writes (operationValueViolation on the view, SCHEMA_VALIDATION_ERROR per op). Every Postgres class-22/23 refusal except 23505 maps to per-op UNSTORABLE_VALUE; SQLite CHECK/NOTNULL/TOOBIG/MISMATCH too. Also found by the new property test: Postgres BIGINT timestamps were read back as strings (fixed in deserializeFieldValue), and the wire decoded json/object values with integer keys and number values (even { " ": 0 }) as bytes and stripped objects containing __kora_bytes__ (fixed in the sync serializer). Tests: repro RT-87 (Postgres), core value-domain.test.ts, server value-domain-ingest.test.ts (memory, SQLite, Postgres), sync wire-value-domain.test.ts, packages/test value-domain-roundtrip.test.ts (seeded random values per field type through memory, SQLite and Postgres server stores, the protobuf wire and a peer client store).

problems.title: The Postgres server store starts initializing in its constructor and nobody holds the promise: an unreachable database is an UNHANDLED rejection (terminates Node by default) while createPostgresServerStore() resolves as if the store were usable
problems.notes: Phase 4 integration, 2026-10-03 (platform engineer's note on the RT-30 merge). Location: server/src/store/postgres-server-store.ts constructor (this.ready = this.initialize(), never awaited until first use) and createPostgresServerStore (returned the store without awaiting ready; the postgres client was never closed on failure). Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-88.test.ts (no Postgres needed: closed local port): before, one unhandledRejection and the factory resolved. FIXED (Phase 4 integration, branch worktree-agent-a59f71e9346b34bbf): the constructor marks the startup promise handled (every method awaits ready and rejects with the error, whenReady() returns it, so nothing is swallowed); createPostgresServerStore awaits whenReady(), ends its client on failure and rejects with ServerStoreUnavailableError (new export, code SERVER_STORE_UNAVAILABLE, host:port/db only, never credentials, driver error as cause). Residual: PostgresServerStore.close() does not end the client createPostgresServerStore opened (pre-existing).

problems.title: With a TokenAuthProvider whose validate() returns no scopes, a sync server without a schema grants the session NOTHING (the claims-only grant binds to no collection and became an empty grant): every write is refused, and the client drops it silently as 'local-only' (no rejection, pendingOperations 0, status 'synced'), with or without encryption
problems.notes: Phase 4 integration, 2026-10-03 (reported by the ENC-1 engineer as 'with token auth no data is uploaded even with encryption off because the server accepted an empty scope'; real, not encryption-related). Locations: server/src/auth/token-auth.ts (no explicit scopes -> claimScopes({ userId })), server/src/scopes/resolve-session-scopes.ts (claims bound only when a schema exists; otherwise grant = {} = nothing visible), server/src/session/client-session.ts (an unscoped resolution left the provider's raw { $claims } grant on the session context, which the upload and delivery checks read: SCOPE_VIOLATION on every op), sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts recordOutOfUplinkScope (a collection absent from the server's accepted scope and from the handshake view was treated as local-only by design: no rejection, no pending count). Repro kora/tests/repro/RT-89.test.ts (createApp + real engine + KoraSyncServer with TokenAuthProvider, schemaless): before, encryption off and on both timed out waiting for the upload. FIXED (Phase 4 integration, branch worktree-agent-a59f71e9346b34bbf): (1) a claims-only grant on a schemaless server is no grant ('unscoped', as the session code's AUTH-1 comment intends for schemaless servers), with a one-time console warning naming the fix (store.setSchema(schema) or explicit scopes); explicit collections in a schemaless grant stay authoritative and a deliberate {} grant still grants nothing; (2) an unscoped resolution strips the raw grant from the session context; (3) client: SyncEngineConfig.syncedCollections (set by createApp from the schema: all collections, or the sync-scoped ones under partial sync rules); without a scope map, a write on a synced collection the server's grant omits is recorded and emitted as OUT_OF_UPLINK_SCOPE instead of silently kept local. Tests: repro RT-89 (3 cases incl. a grant that omits the collection -> visible OUT_OF_UPLINK_SCOPE), server resolve-session-scopes RT-89 unit tests, sync engine 'RT-89: without a scope map...'. Security note: schemaless + token auth now syncs unscoped (each client's handshake narrows its own view), the documented schemaless behavior; multi-tenant deployments must give the server the schema (bindings) or explicit scopes, which the new warning says.

problems.title: A Date inside a t.json() value of a beta.12 write makes its version-1 id unverifiable: beta.12 hashed the Date as {} (canonicalize walks Object.keys) while its log and wire hold the ISO string; an upgraded device uploading a pre-upgrade offline write is refused INVALID_OPERATION_ID and the write is undone on its author
problems.notes: Phase 4 beta.12 compatibility, 2026-10-03 (remediation/evidence/compat-beta12.md). Found against the real published 1.0.0-beta.12 (tag v1.0.0-beta.12 = 91c6350) with scripts/remediation/compat-beta12.mjs; the legacy paths had been built and probed against the never-released Phase 1 build 33bca46. Repro: compat-beta12.mjs upgrade/client-db/offline (1 op of the beta.12 workload refused INVALID_OPERATION_ID after the client database upgrade); packages/server/tests/repro/RT-90.test.ts (3 shapes, protocol-2 upload of a beta.12 op). Through a protocol-1 session the op was stored unverified (RT-71 fallback), so only the upgrade path lost data. Locations: sync/src/engine/verify-inbound.ts matchOperationId (rebuilt undefined members and binary forms only). FIXED: matchOperationId also tries strings in Date#toISOString() form as {} (every combination up to six such strings, all of them above), on every replica (server ingest, duplicate identity, client verification). Such an id never bound the Date value (neither did beta.12), so the match is not declarable: the server stores the op without a declared hash version, as every unverifiable protocol-1 id. Residual: other toJSON objects beta.12 accepted in json values (URL, Luxon/Moment/Decimal instances) are still unverifiable on the upgrade path; documented in compat-beta12.md. Unit tests: sync/src/engine/verify-inbound.test.ts (RT-90 block).

problems.title: After a beta.12 server database is upgraded every anonymous device is refused NODE_ID_CLAIMED even with allowLegacyAnonymousClaims: beta.12 recorded no node claims, and the legacy anonymous path only adopted the pre-release kora:anonymous owner and expired provisional claims
problems.notes: Phase 4 beta.12 compatibility, 2026-10-03 (remediation/evidence/compat-beta12.md). Found against the real published 1.0.0-beta.12 (tag v1.0.0-beta.12 = 91c6350) with scripts/remediation/compat-beta12.mjs; the legacy paths had been built and probed against the never-released Phase 1 build 33bca46. Repro: compat-beta12.mjs upgrade/server-db/{sqlite,postgres}/anonymous (beta.12 device offline for good, its unsynced writes never arrive); packages/server/tests/repro/RT-91.test.ts. Location: server/src/session/client-session.ts claimAnonymousNode (current === null with history -> refused). beta.12 clients cannot rotate their node id, so they reconnect forever. FIXED: with allowLegacyAnonymousClaims a node whose history predates node claims is a legacy anonymous claim: releaseNodeClaim + provisional claim with a token, warning session.legacy_anonymous_claim; never while a session is live as that node; a concurrent claimant loses (and rotates). Signed-in users still cannot take pre-claims history (RT-5 unchanged). Documented residual (types.ts, production-server guide): with MixedAuthProvider an anonymous device can take a signed-in user's beta.12 node, as on beta.12; set allowLegacyAnonymousClaims:false to forbid it (anonymous beta.12 devices are then refused).

problems.title: A database a beta.12 client synced registers its node as accepted (seeded from last_acked_server_vector), so after the server upgrade refuses the node (pre-claims history, RT-5) its offline writes are held forever as other-user, neither assignable nor discardable; the first fix attempt (re-authoring) applied increments the beta.12 server had acknowledged twice
problems.notes: Phase 4 beta.12 compatibility, 2026-10-03 (remediation/evidence/compat-beta12.md). Found against the real published 1.0.0-beta.12 (tag v1.0.0-beta.12 = 91c6350) with scripts/remediation/compat-beta12.mjs; the legacy paths had been built and probed against the never-released Phase 1 build 33bca46. Repro: compat-beta12.mjs upgrade/server-db/{sqlite,postgres}/token (upgraded device's offline write never arrives; status.heldNodes reason other-user); packages/store/tests/repro/RT-92.test.ts. Locations: store/src/sync/local-sync-records.ts hasSyncHistory (accepted from last_acked_server_vector, which assumed the accepting server recorded a claim, true only for claims-aware builds); sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts rotateNodeIdentity -> holdNodeAndSwitch. FIXED: only claims-aware evidence (a node token, the own_acked_through record) seeds accepted; a refused beta.12 node takes the RT-21 never-accepted path, which re-authors only what the beta.12 server never acknowledged: rotateUnsent floors at max(own prefix, last_acked_server_vector[node]) and moves the refused node's prefix to it (without the floor the upgrade re-upload queue was re-authored whole and an increment was applied twice: n=13 instead of 8). Unit tests: store/src/sync/local-sync-records.test.ts (inverted the test that encoded the claims-era assumption), sync/src/engine/local-nodes.test.ts (RT-92 block). beta.12 CLIENTS of an authenticated deployment remain refused until an admin releases their node (RT-5 decision, now documented in production-server.md with the operator procedure). Residual: a beta.12 STORE-1 duplicate at or below the acknowledged entry that the beta.12 server never stored is not re-sent on this path (sequence repair renumbers duplicates above it, so only pairs it kept in place).

problems.title: Through a beta.12 (protocol 1) server, which derives no cascades, a streaming device keeps a provisional cascade of a remote delete until its next reconnect, while devices that received the delete during a catch-up keep the late child: permanent divergence while connected
problems.notes: Phase 4 beta.12 compatibility, 2026-10-03 (remediation/evidence/compat-beta12.md). Found against the real published 1.0.0-beta.12 (tag v1.0.0-beta.12 = 91c6350) with scripts/remediation/compat-beta12.mjs; the legacy paths had been built and probed against the never-released Phase 1 build 33bca46. Repro: compat-beta12.mjs chaos/b12-server (seed 8 of 12: the author of a late child had it deleted provisionally, its peers and a fresh device had it); packages/test/tests/repro/RT-93.test.ts (protocol-1 server simulated: no protocolVersion, no kora: operations). Location: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts recordReceivedBatch (settleAfterCatchUp only while syncing). FIXED together with RT-94 (settle provisional effects after every fully applied final stream batch).

problems.title: With a server of this release, a provisional cascade no server copy confirms (a repeated delete of an already-deleted parent whose late child was revived by later edits) stays applied on a streaming device until its next reconnect, while the server and every peer keep the child
problems.notes: Phase 4 beta.12 compatibility, 2026-10-03 (remediation/evidence/compat-beta12.md). Found against the real published 1.0.0-beta.12 (tag v1.0.0-beta.12 = 91c6350) with scripts/remediation/compat-beta12.mjs; the legacy paths had been built and probed against the never-released Phase 1 build 33bca46. No beta.12 component needed; found by the mixed-fleet chaos matrix (compat-beta12.mjs chaos/current-server, seed 6 of 8: the device that wrote the child kept a provisional delete from a stale device's second delete of the project; the server had stamped its late cascade right after the child's insert, the child's later edits won, and it derived nothing for the second delete). Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-94.test.ts (the effect is left unconfirmed by withholding the server-derived operations from the streaming device; protocol 2). Location: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts recordReceivedBatch. FIXED: a streaming device is caught up after every fully applied final batch and settles provisional effects there (Store.settleAfterCatchUp({ provisionalOnly: true }): row snapshots still settle only at the end of a resync; unit test in store/src/fold/phase3-fold-fixes.test.ts). A server copy is stored with its delete and relayed with it, so confirmed effects are unaffected; one split across a batch boundary shows the child until the next batch. Open question for the cascade owner (not changed here): whether the server should derive a cascade for a delete of an already-deleted parent whose child was revived after the first delete (all replicas now agree the child stays).

problems.title: The recovery public key in the key record is not authenticated: a malicious sync server swaps in its own (push, fetch, or the conflict reply of rotate's compare-and-set) and every later rotate() wraps the new data key to it, so the server reads all operations sealed under that version
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). sync/src/encryption/keyring.ts:349-365 (rotate wraps to record.recovery.publicKey of whatever record was last adopted), keyring.ts:657-760 (adoptLocked checks structure, KDF floor and kept versions only), key-record.ts:131-159 (recovery block is structural only). Repro packages/sync/tests/repro/RT-95.test.ts: the server's own ECDH key unwraps the rotated key and decrypts a sealed op ('secret after-rotation'). Required fix: authenticate the recovery public key with the passphrase KEK (e.g. a KEK-keyed MAC or an AES-GCM wrap whose AAD binds the recovery public key, written by enableRecovery and checked on every adopt), and never wrap a data key to a recovery key that does not verify; a device must also refuse a record whose recovery key changed without that proof. Same class: any record field a device acts on (kdf params, recovery) must be bound to the passphrase holder.

problems.title: A device accepts an older revision of its key record (the rollback pin checks key versions only, never revision): after a passphrase change the server re-serves the old-passphrase revision, the device drops its KEK, only the old (leaked) passphrase unlocks, and the next rotation wraps the new data key under it; the same rollback strips or restores a recovery key
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). sync/src/encryption/keyring.ts:683-701 (pin compares key versions/ids only; a different salt silently drops the KEK), keyring.ts:247 (adoptPushed), key-record.ts isKeyRecordSuccessor (server rule only). Repro packages/sync/tests/repro/RT-96.test.ts. Required fix: pin the highest accepted revision (persisted in the key cache) and refuse lower ones with KEY_RECORD_ROLLBACK; authenticate the record (kdf, recovery, revision) under the KEK so a substituted revision at the same number is detected too. A new device cannot detect a rollback it never saw (document).

problems.title: A rotation that races a passphrase change on another device wraps the new data key under the stale (old-passphrase) KEK into the record with the new salt; every device with the current passphrase then fails WRONG_PASSPHRASE and operations sealed under the new version are readable only on the rotating device
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). sync/src/encryption/keyring.ts:337 (const kek = requireKek(...) read once, outside the compare-and-set loop), keyring.ts:373 (adoptConflictLocked adopts the new-salt record and drops this.kek, the loop keeps the stale local), keyring.ts:697-700. The server cannot tell (it never opens wraps). Repro packages/sync/tests/repro/RT-97.test.ts: a fresh device with the current passphrase is locked WRONG_PASSPHRASE and cannot decrypt the rotating device's op; the passphrase-changing device locks the same way on the push. Required fix: re-read the KEK (requireKek) inside the loop after every conflict adopt, and verify before put that the KEK opens the record's current version under the record's own salt (refuse to wrap under a KEK whose salt differs from record.kdf.salt). Same audit for enableRecovery (it fails loudly today, no corruption).

problems.title: Row changes the syncing tab makes without a new operation (terminal-rejection re-fold, scope retraction/narrowing, provisional cascade settling, authority re-fold) never reach other tabs' live queries: the local operation bus carries only operation:created/applied, so other tabs keep showing the old rows until an unrelated write
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). kora/src/local-operation-bus.ts:52-53 (only operation:created and operation:applied are broadcast); store/src/store/store.ts invalidate-only paths: settleAfterCatchUp (1299), applyProvisionalSideEffects (1359), setAuthoritativeNodeIds (1424), refoldRecordsOf (1457), applyScopeRetraction (1507), and the paths at 2991/3016. Repro kora/tests/repro/RT-98.test.ts: two apps on one better-sqlite3 file (real BroadcastChannel); the server refuses tab A's insert, tab A and tab B's findById return null, tab B's live query keeps the refused todo. With scopes the same path keeps records the user lost access to on screen in other tabs. Required fix: broadcast a collection invalidation (collection names, no payload) from Store whenever it invalidates subscriptions without an operation, and have receivers call subscriptionManager.invalidate; or route every Store invalidate through one hook the bus listens to.

problems.title: The production static server derives ETag, Last-Modified and its compressed-body cache from size and mtime only: a redeployed index.html or sw.js with the same size and a normalised mtime is answered 304 (old shell pointing at deleted chunks; the service worker update is never seen), and a server left running serves the old compressed body
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). server/src/server/static-files.ts:245 (baseTag = size-mtime), :311-327 (isNotModified on that tag or the mtime), :278 (compressed cache key size+mtime). index.html and sw.js keep their byte length across deploys (fixed-length content hashes and VERSION); reproducible/container builds normalise mtimes (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, Nix, Bazel, fixed-date archive extraction). Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-99.test.ts (3 cases). Required fix: content-derived validators for revalidated (no-cache) files: hash the bytes (cache the digest keyed by path+size+mtime+ino+ctime and re-hash when any changes), use it as the ETag and in the compressed-body cache key; do not answer If-Modified-Since alone with 304 for no-cache files whose mtime cannot be trusted (or drop Last-Modified for them).

problems.title: After include(), where() and orderBy() accept the included relation property (e.g. where({ project: null }), orderBy('project')), which the runtime refuses with QueryError 'Unknown field'
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). kora/src/typed-api.ts:177-183 (include returns TypedQueryBuilder<R & Inc[T], Inc>, so TypedWhere<R> and keyof R widen to the relation property); store/src/query/sql-builder.ts:419-434 (validateFieldName). Probe kora/tests/repro/types/RT-100.ts (added to TSC_PROBES): 2 unused @ts-expect-error. Auto fields in insert/update and id in update are correctly refused (lines kept as guards). Required fix: keep the filterable/sortable record type separate from the row type, e.g. TypedQueryBuilder<Row, Inc, Base = R> with where(TypedWhere<Base>) and orderBy(keyof Base & string).

problems.title: Value domain gap: an enum value added by a schema upgrade is valid on every replica, but existing tables keep the old CHECK (col IN (...)): an upgraded device's own write of it throws (SQLite CHECK) and the upgraded server refuses a fresh device's write terminally (UNSTORABLE_VALUE, undone on its author); no migration step can change an enum's values
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). Not a Phase 4 regression (beta.12 has the same DDL). core/src/schema/sql-gen.ts:248,294 (client CHECK), server/src/store/materialization.ts:79-80 and :92-99 (CREATE IF NOT EXISTS + ADD COLUMN only), core/src/migrations/migration-sql.ts (steps: addField/removeField/renameField/addIndex/removeIndex/backfill; nothing for enum values), postgres-server-store.ts:173-176 and sqlite-server-store.ts:171-173 (23514 / SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_CHECK -> UNSTORABLE_VALUE). Repro kora/tests/repro/RT-101.test.ts (device: CHECK constraint failed: priority; SQLite server: sync:operation-rejected UNSTORABLE_VALUE). Postgres the same by code (23514). Required fix: enforce enum membership in the value domain (validateRecord) only, not in DDL (drop the CHECK, or rebuild it from the current schema on open: SQLite table rebuild, Postgres ALTER TABLE DROP/ADD CONSTRAINT), on client and server stores; or add an explicit migration step that rebuilds the constraint and refuse a schema whose enum values changed without it. Also decide what a REMOVED enum value means for existing rows and old-schema ops (transform or keep accepting).

problems.title: The query-store cache and useQuery's re-subscribe key are JSON.stringify(descriptor), which drops undefined (and folds NaN into null): where({ projectId: undefined }) shares one QueryStore with where({}) although the runtime returns different rows, so one of two mounted components renders the other's results
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). store/src/reactivity/query-store-cache.ts:62 (getKey), react/src/hooks/use-query.ts:51 (descriptorKey); the same key pattern in the Vue/Svelte bindings should be checked. store/src/query/sql-builder.ts:299-321 binds the undefined value ('"projectId" = ?'), so the two queries differ at runtime. Repro kora/tests/repro/RT-102.test.ts (control: exec results differ; the cache returns the same store). Required fix: normalise the where clause once in QueryBuilder.where (decide what undefined means: drop the condition, or IS NULL, and refuse NaN), so the descriptor, the SQL and the key agree; derive the key from that canonical descriptor.

problems.title: Retiring an old schema transform (registering v2->v3 but no longer v1->v2) silently erases every v1 operation from the server's records at the next start: the fingerprint change re-folds everything, operationSchemaView returns null for ops with no path, and mergeOp folds null as nothing (no error, log or quarantine); removing the whole list instead keeps them
problems.notes: Final RC red team (remediation/evidence/redteam-rc.md). core/src/fold/fold.ts:409-410 (null view folds as nothing), core/src/migration/operation-view.ts:55-60 (an empty list folds as written, a partial list returns null), server/src/store/record-fold.ts:130-139, fold plan fingerprint includes transforms (re-fold on change). docs/guide/schema-design.md asks to keep transforms 'as long as operations of its source version can exist', which is forever for an append-only log, and nothing enforces it. Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-103.test.ts (SQLite server store; the v1 record is null after the restart). Devices: by code reading the same null view at a re-fold drops the op from their records too. Required fix: at setSchema/open, refuse (OperationTransformError naming the versions) a transform set that has no path from a schema version present in the stored log to the current one; and treat a null view of a STORED op as quarantine/keep-as-written, never as an absent op (a transform returning null deliberately is a separate, explicit decision that should be logged).
